purpose: Exact small-domain regression fixture for permutation randomization QA; tests a concrete full-law diagnostic, not the new asymptotic upper bound or a new shuffle algorithm.
hypothesis: For N=4 and N=8, after d=log2(N) physical Thorp shuffles and under a uniform random cyclic shift, every one-card marginal passes an exact uniformity audit while the full permutation law has TV>1/4. A support-obstruction audit flags all four under-mixed regimes and has zero false alarms on exhaustive Fisher-Yates reference laws. N=2 is a boundary control.

input.coin_model: independent fair pair coins; all coin outcomes enumerated and probabilities aggregated as integer path counts
input.source_frame: MSB-first positions; physical step (b,u)->(u,b XOR coin[u]); permutation maps card labels to positions

baseline: Exact marginal-only audit versus cheap support-size lower-bound audit; exact exhaustive Fisher-Yates is the already sufficient uniform sampler, not an algorithm claimed to be improved by Thorp.
judge: Exact Fraction TV against uniform S_N, including absent permutations; all-card marginals and first-two-card joint laws. Independently implement physical split/interleave semantics for all N=4 starting decks and coins.
failure: Any transition mismatch, invalid probability/permutation, support lower bound above exact TV, failure to flag any of the four declared under-mixed regimes, or any Fisher-Yates false alarm.
limits: Synthetic N<=8 fixture. Does not validate 1600d asymptotics, compute a finite-N upper guarantee from that theorem, establish cryptographic security, improve Fisher-Yates, or justify large-domain factorial enumeration. Expected obstruction is already elementary; incremental benefit from the new optimal-order theorem remains unshown.
